I hear you, spirit of the night. If there are folk at Wewush with empty bellies, and they are not too far, we have wheat enough in our granary to spare some. Yet dreams are shifting smoke; tell me truly where to find them when the sun is high, and we will see what can be done.
My granary is heavy with wheat, spirit, and needs no planting now. It is the meat and the fish that grow thin when the winter comes. Why do you bid me turn the earth while the leaves are falling?

The wind blows through my head while I sleep, but wind leaves no tracks in the dirt. Joawethom is a name I do not know, and strangers who ask for food often bring trouble to our hearth. If there are people in need, let them come and trade for what we have grown with our own backs and hands; we give nothing for shadows in the night.
